1.

The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Govind Babu,
aged about 19 years, suffered grievous injury.
An application u/s 166(1) Motor Vehicle Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant seeking compensation.

A separate claim petition was filed with respect to the same accident by another vehicle Vivek with MACT No. 1096/24.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that on 31.01.2022 at about 08:00 a.m., victim Govind Babu (as a pillion rider) along with one Vivek Kumar, was going towards Kanpur Govind Babu vs Surender Kumar on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2525352/
1 from District Etawa on the motorcycle bearing no.UP-75AM-3179.
The motorcycle was being driven by Vivek Kumar.

When they reached in front of Kanchan Hotel Sikandra, a speeding truck coming from Orreya bearing no.HR-69B-6768 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle) came at a high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle.
Due to the collision both fell on the road and sustained injuries.
They were removed to the Zila Chikitsalaya Akbarpur where victim Govind sustained injuries and leg of the victim Vivek got amputed.
3. An FIR no.0036/2022 date 01.03.2022 was registered u/s 279,337/338/427 of IPC, PS Sikandra, Distt-Kanpur Dehat, U.P.
Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while the present claim petition was filed by petitioner Govind Babu.

4. Respondent no.1 is driver cum owner and respondent no.2 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was MACT No.412/25 Govind Babu vs.
Surender Kumar & anr. P.No. 2 of 10 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.05.07 16:10:24 +0530 insured.
5. Written statement was filed by respondent no. 1 denying rash and negligence on the part of respondent no.1.
It has been pleaded that respondent no.1 was having a valid driving licence.

In its reply respondent no.2/insurance company has denied its liability to indemnify the insured /respondent no.1 or compensate the petitioner in case respondents were found to be in breach of the insurance policy.

6. Vide order dated 11.09.2024, following issues were framed.
1.
Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 31.01.2022 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR69B-6768 being driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2?
OPP 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP.

10. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under:
Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 31.01.2022 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR69B-6768 being driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2?
OPP 11.

Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable.
Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors.

sentences.text: 12. In the instant case, respondents have taken a defence as to the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

In order to prove, the involvement of the offending vehicle petitioner examined himself as PW-1 wherein he testified that the accident took place when the motorcycle which was being driven by victim Vivek Kumar was hit from behind by the offending truck.
PW1 has no where testified that he had seen the offending vehicle or noted its number.

sentences.text: Despite this fact, the registration number of the offending vehicle was never disclosed by the victim or the driver of the motorcycle, at the first instance even to the doctor who examined them.
None of the medical documents mentions the registration number of the offending vehicle.

Though furnishing of details of the alleged vehicle may not be mandatory to be disclosed to the treating doctor, it is crucial that such details must have been informed to the police at least, soon after the accident.
In the present case, the FIR has been registered after a delay of almost three months from the accident.

Despite the fact that both the victim were in a conscious state and also accompanied by family members of victim Vivek during his treatment, the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle was never disclosed.

Such non-disclosure of the information and details of the offending vehicle coupled with the fact that even the mechanical inspection report of the involved vehicle has not been placed, further renders involvement of such vehicle doubtful.
This is particularly so as the driver of the alleged offending vehicle has also led evidence testifying that his vehicle was never involved in any accident as alleged by the petitioner.

Respondent no.1, testifying as RW-1 has also stated that it is only pursuant to a call received on 28.03.2022 from mobile no. 7571830066 by someone introducing himself as Sanjesh Kumar,
investigating officer from police station Sikandra that the respondent was informed about involvement of his vehicle in the accident.

He has further deposed that even his TIP was never conducted by the concerned police and thus, there was nothing to establish the identity of the vehicle involved in the MACT No.412/25 Govind Babu vs.

sentences.text: During cross examination RW1 further denied that the offending truck was ever seized by the police or released on superdari.
Petitioner has filed no evidence on record to show that the offending truck was seized by the police or if seized, the date of the same.
It is pertinent to note that in the alleged accident it was not only the petitioner /victim Govind who suffered injuries but also one Vivek who allegedly got injured.
In fact, a referral slip issued by Sanyukt Zila Chikitsalaya qua the treatment of victim Govind also does not mention the details of the vehicle.

Such medical slip does not reveal any medical condition of Govind Babu preventing him from disclosing the details of the offending vehicle for 3 months, despite the fact that he was discharged from such hospital on the same day.

Also there is no continuity in the treatment record relied upon by victim Govind Babu which leads to an inference that the details of the actual offending vehicle may not have been known or noted by either of the victims.
Respondents have also examined the owner of the offending vehicle as R1W2 who has testified that he had accompanied driver of the offending vehicle to the police station on 04.04.2022.

It is observed that despite denial by driver as well as the owner of the offending vehicle qua the involvement of the alleged vehicle, no document has been produced or evidence has been led to show the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

sentences.text: 13. In these circumstances, though there is no evidence to the contrary to disbelieve the occurrence of the accident, there is serious and considerable doubt in believing that such an accident was caused by the offending vehicle.
It is possible that the offending vehicle may not have been identified and may have remained untrace and only to secure compensation, details of the offending vehicle may have been planted later on.
As such, instead of dismissing the case, the present petition is being treated as a case of offending vehicle remaining untraced.
Issue no.2
Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP.
14.
For the reason discussed in issue no.1, claimants are held not entitled to any compensation from the respondents.
Issue no.2 is accordingly decided against the petitioners/claimants.
However, since only the involvement of the offending vehicle is not proved but probability of occurrence of the accident is proved, the case may be treated as a case where the offender is not traced.

As per Section 396(4) of (BNSS) Baratiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita:
